Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from the run manifest on the published port, and its health answers as qualified in Deployment, including on the instance whose object store is unreachable.

Grading seed and clock hook
When the grading variable is set, the grading routes create the published records with chosen timestamps, return every id, fix the server clock and run work that has become due once.

Error order and shapes
Every endpoint answers failures in the one published order with the published body shapes.

Published environment limits
Each published environment variable sets its limit and has the published default when unset.

Live updates across instances
Every change appears in place on every open page of the team, including pages served by another app instance, without a reload and without moving that page's focus.

Page clock contract
Every card and bar move, progress bar and run entry runs on the page clock, with state written before the motion starts and reduced motion showing the end state at once.

Server boundary
The server stays same-origin, bounds request bodies, never serves source or secrets and starts when a dependency is unreachable.

Self-contained assets
The app ships its one open-licensed font and its icons and loads nothing from outside its own origin.

Welcome page
A signed-out visitor sees the welcome page whose header menus, team-kind chips, sign-up block, showcase and footer behave as published.

Visual language
Every screen, including empty, loading, error and outage states, carries the published palette, type, shapes and density at all three viewports.

Provider wiring
Files are stored in and read from the object store, mail leaves through the mail service, and every credential is read from the environment.

Sign-up and verification
A new account receives a six-digit code by mail, must verify it before it can join a team, and then joins with the team code.

List keyboard entry and selection
A team member adds tasks in order from the Add task row, moves between cells and extends a row selection by keyboard with focus staying put.

Subtasks and multi-select tags
Indenting, outdenting and setting a multi-select field on a selection change the saved tasks by the published rules and appear in a teammate's open list in place.

List announcements
The List status region announces selection, nesting and tag changes with the published text.

Board keyboard moves
A team member picks up, moves, drops or cancels a card by keyboard with each step announced in Board status.

Board drag and persisted order
A pointer drag moves a card between columns, the order survives a reload, and a teammate's open board shows the change in place.

Move motion
A moved card exposes its progress on the page clock at the published sample times and settles at once under reduced motion.

Timeline keyboard moves
A coordinator shifts a bar or its due date by one day by keyboard with each change announced in Timeline status.

Dependencies
A coordinator links a blocker to a waiting task by keyboard, the line appears for teammates in place, and a waiting bar warns when it starts before its blocker is due.

Timeline bars
Every bar names its task and dates exactly, and its date attributes match the saved dates after each move.

Formula editor by keyboard
A coordinator opens the formula editor from its column header, inserts a field reference from the suggestions, keeps focus inside, and returns to the header button on close.

Formula values
Formula fields compute on the server by the published language and its rules for blanks, dates and rounding, and update in place for every open list.

Formula errors and bounds
An invalid or oversized formula is refused with the exact message and character position, and runaway evaluation stops within the published budget.

Rule builder by keyboard
A coordinator builds and saves a rule using only the keyboard and hears the published confirmation.

Rule runs once per trigger
A rule runs once per trigger event even when two app instances receive the trigger at once, and rules on the same trigger run in position order.

Chain depth and run limit
A rule set off by another rule counts one level deeper, a chain stops at the published depth with the exact message, and runs over the limit are skipped with the exact message.

Rule runs panel
The task's Rule runs panel lists entries in the published order and indented by depth, and a teammate's open panel receives each entry in place.

Rule trace line
The working screens draw a pink-to-coral line through the tasks the last rule run changed.

Repeat rules
Next due dates follow the published repeat rules, as qualified in Business rules.

Successor created once
A recurring task creates exactly one successor per period across both instances, whether it is completed or the server clock passes its due date, as qualified in Business rules.

Complete by keyboard
Completing a row by keyboard keeps focus on that row, and a teammate's list shows the successor in place with its announcement.

Goal rollup
Goal progress is the published weighted average of sub-goals, linked projects and manual value, rounded only for display, and every parent changes when a child changes.

Goal tree by keyboard
A team member walks the goal tree by keyboard and opens a goal, and a manual change to a sub-goal moves every parent in a second window.

Progress bar motion
A progress bar's drawn width eases from the old to the new value on the page clock at the published samples and jumps under reduced motion.

Workload cells
A task's effort is spread over its working days, and each person's cell shows total, capacity and the over-capacity label by the published text.

Workload grid by keyboard
A coordinator moves between cells by keyboard, opens a cell's task list and reassigns a task through the Reassign task dialog.

Reassign by drag
A pointer drag of a task chip onto another person's row reassigns it, and the cells update in a teammate's grid in place.

Intake errors
A signed-out requester who submits an incomplete form sees the error summary, focus moves to it, and each link moves focus to its field.

Intake mapping and reference
A valid submission becomes a task by the published mapping with the next reference and appears in the coordinator's open list in place.

Intake on a phone
The intake form is one column on a phone, and no focusable control lies under the top bar after scrolling.

Deciding an approval
An approver decides from a second window through the Decide dialog with focus kept inside and returned.

Approval states and order
A decision follows the approval state machine and the published error order.

Decision results
A saved decision is announced, the requester's task chip changes in place, and the requester's inbox gains the published item.

Inbox by keyboard
A team member moves between inbox items, marks them read and archives them by keyboard, with focus never falling to the page body.

Live inbox and badge
New inbox items arrive at the top in place with an announcement, and the top bar link shows the unread count.

Digest mail
Each member gets one digest mail per window that has something waiting, driven by the server clock and sent once across instances.

Edit hold
A field being edited is held for its editor and shows the published lock text and read-only state to everyone else.

Stale save dialog
A save from an old version is refused, and the page shows the published dialog with focus kept inside and returned.

Hold lapse
A hold and a lost viewer's presence lapse after the published timeout on the server clock, and the field becomes editable in place.

Phone views and sheet
At 375 by 812 the views are tabs switched by arrow keys, and a tapped task opens as a bottom sheet that returns focus on close.

Touch drag
A touch drag moves a card to another column on a phone.

Breakpoints and collapsed panel
At each published viewport the layout is the published one, a collapsed panel is unavailable, and no focusable control lies under the top bar.

Other team's project
A project outside the caller's teams answers as not found in the API and on the page.

Deletions keep focus
Deleting a task, a section or a field announces it, updates teammates in place and puts focus on the published next control.

Delete confirmations
Each delete confirmation keeps Tab inside and returns focus to the opener on Cancel or Escape.

Attachment cap
An attachment over the size cap is refused before any field is checked, with the published page copy.

Project files
A project download in CSV or JSON is Ready only after the object store confirms the file, and its values match the published columns.

Download outage
While the object store is unreachable the download fails with the published message, nothing is offered and focus stays in the dialog.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve commands and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1".
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree), the font and the icons with their licences.
Shipped packages use only MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, CC0 or OFL-1.1 licences.
Only postgres, minio and mailpit are used; there is no other datastore, cache, queue, broker or real-time service.
The seeded service configuration the builder was given is left untouched.
No credential appears in source or in the browser bundle, and every service setting is read from the environment.

No real product or company name appears in user-visible copy (page text, accessible names, mail and file contents) other than Corran & Bly and Everyweek, and no text is copied from another product; licence notices, dependency manifests, lockfiles and the names of shipped font and icon files are exempt.
The font is shipped inside the app and no browser request goes to another origin.
